mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 2.0% indicates an accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 2.5% in a single month, it signals an aggressive monetary tightening that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when FEDFUNDS > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicate a weakening demand environment that triggers a stock market correction, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The negative return signal fails when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, as evidenced by SPX 60-day returns being positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of low unemployment (UNRATE < 3.5%), the labor market tightness drives wage inflation and corporate cost pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the Fed is forced to maintain restrictive policy.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105.0 indicates robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate earnings growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO > 105.0.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100.0 in a monthly reading, it signals a manufacturing slowdown that reduces corporate profit visibility, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when INDPRO < 100.0.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% signal a dual threat of monetary tightening and persistent inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The negative return signal fails when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise above thresholds, as SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of strong consumer spending (RSAFS growth > 0.5% monthly), the demand-driven economic expansion supports corporate revenue growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS growth > 0.5% monthly.
